things_that_must_work: The lightweight desktop sensors must reliably capture accurate and comprehensive work pattern data without significant performance impact or privacy concerns.
The "Intelligence Layer" must accurately detect employee intent, business value, and workflow drift with high precision and recall.
The "Agent Factory" must be able to automatically generate and deploy effective AI agents that deliver on validated high-ROI opportunities.
Existing foundation models must be adaptable and performant enough to be leveraged effectively by Narma’s system.
Enterprises must be willing to adopt a system that extensively observes employee work patterns.

market_data.trigger_now: Enterprises often struggle with a lack of telemetry to pinpoint AI savings, unreliable ROI measurements, and constant drift in systems and human resources.

core_insight.why_different: Narma focuses on the entire lifecycle of AI automation from observation to agent deployment and continuous optimization, rather than just providing AI models or fragmented solutions. Its 'Work Graph' approach and 'Agent Factory' are key differentiators.
core_insight.if_wrong: If companies cannot achieve accurate observation, reliable intent/drift detection, or effective automated agent deployment, then the system will fail to provide scalable AI automation and continuous AI lift.

raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" with a three-layered architecture. Layer 1 (Observe) uses lightweight desktop sensors to capture work patterns (application usage, activity sequences, time allocation). Layer 2 (Intelligence Layer) is a "Brain" that detects employee intent, business value of tasks, and workflow "drift." Layer 3 (Execution Layer) is an "Agent Factory" that generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for high-ROI opportunities with built-in approval gates. It leverages existing foundation models and focuses on the "Work Graph" to identify areas for AI intervention, providing a continuous AI lift.

raw.thesis: Narma is building an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" to enable AI-first companies to effectively deploy AI automation at scale. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: observing work patterns via desktop sensors (Layer 1), an "Intelligence Layer" that detects employee intent, business value of tasks, and "drift" in workflows (Layer 2), and an "Agent Factory" that generates and deploys AI agents for high-ROI opportunities (Layer 3). This system focuses on uncovering the "Work Graph" to identify inefficiencies and opportunities for AI intervention, rather than developing new foundation models. It aims to provide a continuous AI uplift by observing, deciding, and automatically building agents. This venture is for AI-first companies struggling with the lack of telemetry to measure AI savings, unreliable ROI, and workflow drift. The founder’s goal is to establish a growth startup that provides a single system for continuous AI optimization. Based on the description, the venture is currently at the idea stage, with a clear concept and architectural design but no mention of a built product or users. The venture aims to replace fragmented approaches to AI automation and ROI measurement with a cohesive, end-to-end system that provides continuous intelligence and autonomous agent deployment.

bottleneck.why_it_blocks: Without a built product, the core claims of observation, intelligence, and agent deployment cannot be tested or validated.
bottleneck.relaxed_by: Developing a functional prototype or MVP of the three-layered architecture, starting with the observation layer.
